long_biography.plain_text:
Callimanopulos began in his father's liner business before striking out from New York in his mid-twenties to establish Trade & Transport. The venture grew through tramp shipping and tankers, giving him an independently built operating base before he inherited control of Hellenic Lines. As managing director, he tried to modernise the family carrier around container ships during a severe industry downturn.

After Hellenic Lines closed, Callimanopulos expanded again through Marine Management Services and Toisa, assembling fleets in tankers, dry bulk and technically demanding offshore support. He remained Toisa's chairman and sole owner, with final authority over chartering, and accumulated more than five decades as a shipowner. The group's later bankruptcy reduced his fleet but did not erase the separate company-building record that preceded and followed the inherited liner business.
